Bytes que InnoDB leyó de sus archivos; i: Bytes InnoDB read from its files; includes what the operating system cache resolves. If it rises together with a drop in the buffer pool hit rate, the data does not fit in memory.
Bytes que PostgreSQL escribió desde sus: Bytes PostgreSQL wrote from its buffers to the table and index files (temporary tables too), without the WAL or the sort temporary files. Requires PostgreSQL 16 or later.
Bytes que PostgreSQL leyó fuera de share: Bytes PostgreSQL read from outside shared_buffers, from disk or from the operating system cache.
Bytes que WiredTiger escribió en los arc: Bytes WiredTiger wrote to the data files (checkpoints and eviction of modified pages), not counting the journal.
Bytes que WiredTiger leyó de los archivo: Bytes WiredTiger read from the data files because they were not cached. A high, sustained rate indicates the cache is not enough for the data being queried.
Bytes que el servidor envió a los client: Bytes the server sent to clients.
Bytes que el servidor envió a todos los: Bytes the server sent to all clients. A jump usually comes from queries that return many rows.
Bytes que el servidor envió por la red,: Bytes the server sent over the network, to clients and to other replicas.
Bytes que el servidor envió por la red:: Bytes the server sent over the network: results to clients and replication to the other members.
Bytes que el servidor escribió en disco:: Bytes the server wrote to disk: new parts, merges and logs. If the system does not report real I/O (OSWriteBytes), these are file writes.
Bytes que el servidor escribió en la red: Bytes the server wrote to the network: responses to clients. Much more than incoming network usually points to reads of large values or collections.
Bytes que el servidor le pidió a jemallo: Bytes the server requested from jemalloc and still uses. The difference from resident memory is allocator metadata, fragmentation and free pages not yet returned to the system.
Bytes que el servidor leyó de la red: lo: Bytes the server read from the network: the clients' commands with their arguments.
Bytes que el servidor leyó del disco. Si: Bytes the server read from disk. If the system does not report real I/O (OSReadBytes), these are file reads, which include what the operating system cache resolves.
Bytes que el servidor recibió de los cli: Bytes the server received from clients.
Bytes que el servidor recibió de todos l: Bytes the server received from all clients.
Bytes que el servidor recibió por la red: Bytes the server received over the network, from clients and from other replicas.
Bytes the server received over the network: client requests and traffic from the other cluster members.
Bytes que envió la máquina del DataNode: Bytes sent by the DataNode's machine over all its network interfaces except loopback, so it includes other processes' traffic.
Bytes que envió por la red la máquina de: Bytes sent over the network by the machine of this session's node, from all its processes and interfaces.
Bytes que escribieron los discos de la m: Bytes written by the disks of the DataNode's machine, summing all devices, so it includes other processes' activity.
Bytes que escribieron todos los procesos: Bytes written by all the server's processes (checkpointer, bgwriter, sessions, autovacuum), data and WAL. Does not include the temporary files of sorts and hashes.
Bytes que este miembro envió a los clien: Bytes this member sent to clients over gRPC: responses and watch events. Does not include traffic between members.
Bytes que este miembro recibió de los cl: Bytes this member received from clients over gRPC. Does not include traffic between cluster members.
Bytes que la VM Erlang envió por sus pue: Bytes the Erlang VM sent through its ports: mostly responses to clients and traffic to the other cluster nodes.
Bytes que la VM Erlang recibió por sus p: Bytes the Erlang VM received through its ports: mostly network traffic from clients and from the other cluster nodes.
Bytes que la base actual escribió en dis: Bytes the current database wrote to disk: pages times the page size.
Bytes que la base actual leyó del disco:: Bytes the current database read from disk: pages times the page size.
Bytes que la base envió a los clientes p: Bytes the database sent to clients over SQL*Net, mostly result rows.
Bytes the database sent to clients over TCP/IP.
Bytes que la base escribió en su archivo: Bytes the database wrote to its file: pages written, times the page size.
Bytes que la base leyó de su archivo: pá: Bytes the database read from its file: pages that were not in the cache, times the page size. Includes what the operating system cache resolves.
Bytes que la base recibió de los cliente: Bytes the database received from clients over SQL*Net: statements, parameters and data being loaded.
Bytes the database received from clients over TCP/IP.
Bytes que las consultas volcaron a archi: Bytes queries spilled to temporary files because a sort or a hash did not fit in work_mem. If it grows often, review those queries or raise work_mem.
Bytes que leyeron las consultas de las r: Bytes the queries read from the regions, from memory or from disk.
Bytes que leyeron los discos de la máqui: Bytes read by the disks of the DataNode's machine, summing all devices, so it includes other processes' activity.
Bytes que leyeron todos los procesos del: Bytes read by all the server's processes (sessions, autovacuum, background processes), data and WAL. These are reads requested from the operating system: some may come from its cache without touching the disk.
Bytes que los OBServer enviaron por RPC,: Bytes the OBServers sent over RPC, the internal network between the cluster nodes; it is not client traffic.
Bytes que los OBServer escribieron en di: Bytes the OBServers wrote to disk for the tenants this user can see.
Bytes que los OBServer leyeron del disco: Bytes the OBServers read from disk for the tenants this user can see.
Bytes que los OBServer recibieron por RP: Bytes the OBServers received over RPC, the internal network between the cluster nodes; it is not client traffic.
Bytes que ocupan en memoria los puntos r: Bytes taken in memory by recently written points not yet flushed to TSM files, summed across shards. Grows with the write rate; if a shard reaches cache-max-memory-size, InfluxDB rejects writes.

Bytes taken in memory by recently written points not yet flushed to TSM files, summed across shards. Grows with the write rate; if a shard reaches storage-cache-max-memory-size, InfluxDB rejects writes.
Bytes que ocupan las tablas de todas las: Bytes taken by the tables of all databases (in MergeTree, compressed on disk). The maximum is the size of the configured disks, which may also hold other files.
Bytes que ocupan los registros guardados: Bytes taken by the records stored in the current database's clusters. Does not include indexes, the WAL or the files' reserved space, so what the database takes on disk is considerably more.
Bytes que recibió la máquina del DataNod: Bytes received by the DataNode's machine over all its network interfaces except loopback, so it includes other processes' traffic.
Bytes que recibió por la red la máquina: Bytes received over the network by the machine of this session's node, from all its processes and interfaces.
Bytes que se cobran con precios on-deman: Bytes billed at on-demand prices for the jobs finished in the last 15 minutes: they are rounded up (minimum 10 MB per table) and what comes from the cache is not billed. With slot reservations you pay for capacity, not these bytes.
Bytes recibidos por la capa de transport: Bytes received by the transport layer between nodes (replication, shard recovery, distributed searches), summed across nodes. Does not include clients' HTTP traffic; with a single node it stays near zero.
Búsquedas de claves (GET, HGET y demás l: Key lookups (GET, HGET and other reads) that found the requested key.
Búsquedas de claves que encontraron la c: Key lookups that found the key, over total lookups, accumulated since startup or the last CONFIG RESETSTAT, so it moves slowly. Low is normal if the application looks up keys that do not exist; in a cache it means keys expire or are evicted too soon.
Búsquedas de claves que no la encontraro: Key lookups that did not find it: it does not exist, expired or was evicted.
Búsquedas de series que la caché de esqu: Series lookups that the DataNode's schema cache resolved without going to the schema region, accumulated since it started. Low and sustained slows writes and queries; memory for the schema may be lacking.
Búsquedas que atendió searchd, por cualq: Searches handled by searchd, over any protocol.
Búsquedas que se respondieron desde la c: Searches answered from the result cache, without running again.

Carpeta con los .dbf (o uno de sus archi: Folder with the .dbf files (or one of its files)

Cassandra no expone el uso de CPU ni la: Cassandra doesn't expose CPU usage or JVM memory over CQL; that requires JMX (nodetool info / tpstats).

Catálogo al que se cambia después de con: Catalog to switch to after connecting.
Checkpoints, por tiempo (checkpoint_time: Checkpoints, timed (checkpoint_timeout) or requested (by max_wal_size or a CHECKPOINT). If there is more than one every few minutes, max_wal_size is usually too small for the write load.
Chunks (particiones por intervalo de tie: Chunks (partitions by time interval) of all the hypertables in this database. Many small chunks make query planning more expensive: review chunk_time_interval.

Clientes con un feed _changes continuo a: Clients with a continuous _changes feed open on this node, such as syncing apps or replications reading from it.

CockroachDB solo muestra las consultas e: CockroachDB only shows running queries for the whole cluster.
Colecciones definidas en el cluster de S: Collections defined in the SolrCloud cluster.

Space used on the nodes' data disks, summed; the maximum is their capacity. Past the watermarks (85 %, 90 % and 95 % by default) the cluster stops allocating shards to the node, moves them and, at the last, makes its indexes read-only.

Memoria en uso de las máquinas de los dn: Memory in use on the dnodes' machines (total minus free), summed across them. It counts the operating system's file cache as used, so it often looks high even with memory available.
Memoria en uso de las máquinas de los no: Memory in use on the nodes' machines, by all their processes (total minus available), summed across nodes.

Memoria física del equipo en uso por tod: Physical memory of the machine in use by all processes, according to the operating system. If little is left available, the system asks SQL Server to release memory.
Memoria física del equipo menos la libre: Physical memory of the machine minus the free, according to the operating system, for all processes. It may include the system file cache, so seeing it almost full is not always a lack of memory.
Memoria física en uso en el servidor, de: Physical memory in use on the server, by all processes; the maximum is the total memory.
Memoria física en uso en los hosts, de t: Physical memory in use on the hosts, by all processes (HANA included); the maximum is the total physical memory.
Memoria física ocupada en la máquina (to: Physical memory taken on the machine (total minus free), out of the total, according to the JVM. It includes Neo4j's page cache, the heap, other processes and the operating system's file cache, so it is often near the total even when memory is not lacking.
Memoria física que el sistema operativo: Physical memory the operating system assigns to the process. It adds fragmentation and what the allocator has not returned yet, so it is usually larger than the used memory.
Memoria física que ocupa el proceso de S: Physical memory the SQL Server process takes (working set, large pages and AWE included), with what it reserves outside the memory manager. The maximum is the machine's memory.
Memoria física que ocupa el proceso etcd: Physical memory the etcd process takes. It grows with keys, the uncompacted revision history and watchers.
Memoria física que ocupan las páginas de: Physical memory taken by jemalloc's pages, the allocator that handles almost all the process's memory. If it approaches the machine's RAM or the container limit, the system may kill the process.
Memoria física usada en la máquina de es: Physical memory used on this server's machine. It includes the operating system's file cache, which Solr uses to read the indexes, so it is often high without being a problem.
Memoria física usada en las máquinas de: Physical memory used on the nodes' machines, summed. It includes the operating system's file cache, which the engine uses to read the indexes, so it is often high without being a problem.
Memoria ocupada en los hosts del cluster: Memory taken on the cluster's hosts (total minus free, summing the nodes), out of their total memory. Includes that of other processes on those hosts.

Memory reserved by queries in the general pool of the whole cluster, out of its size on all nodes. Near the maximum, new queries wait or are cancelled for lack of memory.

Tablets (las porciones en que se reparte: Tablets (the portions the data is split into) the backends store, replicas included. Many small tablets load the nodes' memory and metadata.
Tamaño de la buffer cache, la parte de l: Size of the buffer cache, the part of the SGA that holds data blocks. With automatic memory management, Oracle enlarges or shrinks it according to load.
Tamaño de las claves y valores que guard: Size of the keys and values stored by tables, materialized views and jobs' internal state in RisingWave's storage.
Tamaño de las tablas dBase de la carpeta: Size of the folder's dBase tables: data files, indexes and memos.
Tamaño de las tablas de esta base, sumad: Size of this database's tables, summed, from the latest hourly measurement.
Tamaño de las tablas de la región, sumad: Size of the region's tables, summed across the first 100. DynamoDB updates it roughly every six hours, so it does not follow writes instantly.
Tamaño de los HFiles de las regiones abi: Size of the HFiles of the regions open on the RegionServers, summed, not counting HDFS replication.
Tamaño del archivo de la base en disco,: Size of the database file on disk, out of the backend quota. On reaching the quota, etcd raises the NOSPACE alarm and accepts only reads and deletes until it is compacted, defragmented and the alarm is cleared.
Tamaño del archivo de la base: páginas a: Size of the database file: allocated pages times page size, including the free ones left inside. The file does not shrink on its own; to recover space, back up and restore.
Tamaño máximo de la caché de páginas de: Maximum size of each connection's page cache: it is a limit, not what is in use.
Tareas asíncronas vivas en los runtimes: Live asynchronous tasks in the Tokio runtimes: queries, writes, connections and internal jobs. If they grow without stopping under steady load, work is left hanging.
Tareas detenidas porque la cola de su po: Tasks stopped because their thread pool's queue is full, like "Blocked" in nodetool tpstats. Non-zero indicates the node is saturated.
Tareas en cola en los pools de hilos del: Queued tasks in the node's thread pools, waiting for a free thread. If they pile up (especially in ReadStage, MutationStage or CompactionExecutor), the node cannot keep up.
Tareas en segundo plano que corren ahora: Background tasks running now in the cluster: view indexing, compactions and replications. Many at once compete with requests for disk and CPU.
Tareas que esperan un hilo libre, sumada: Tasks waiting for a free thread, summed across all thread pools and nodes. A sustained queue indicates a saturated pool; when it fills up, tasks are rejected.
Tareas que terminó el pool de compactaci: Tasks the node's compaction pool finished: compactions and other operations on SSTables.
Tareas que un thread pool rechazó porque: Tasks a thread pool rejected because its queue was full, summed across pools and nodes. Each rejection is a search or a write that failed with 429; the thread pools table shows which one saturates.

Tiempo de CPU del proceso de Solr como p: CPU time of the Solr process as a percentage of the processors the JVM can use: 100 % is all busy. Sustained high, searches and indexing compete for CPU.
Tiempo de CPU del proceso del servidor c: CPU time of the server process as a share of the logical processors it uses: 100 % equals all busy.
Tiempo de CPU del proceso influxd (usuar: CPU time of the influxd process (user and system) as a percentage of all the cores the server sees: 100 % is all busy. Sustained near 100 %, queries and writes compete for CPU.
Tiempo de CPU que consume el proceso de: CPU time the Neo4j process consumes, as a share of all the cores the JVM can use: 100 % is all busy. Compared with the server's CPU, it shows how much of that load is Neo4j's.
Tiempo de CPU que consumen los procesos: CPU time the engine's processes consume on all nodes, as a share of all their cores: 100 % is all busy. Compared with the cluster's CPU, it shows how much of that load is the engine's.
Tiempo de CPU que gastaron las consultas: CPU time the queries spent, as a share of all the cluster's cores: 100 % is all busy. Each query adds its whole CPU seconds when it finishes: those under a second do not count, and a long one appears all at once at the end and may exceed 100 % for a moment.
CPU time the queries spent, as a share of all the cluster's cores: 100 % is all busy. Compared with the processes' CPU, it shows how much goes to queries and how much to the rest of the engine.

CPU time the queries spent, in CPU seconds: one second per second is one core busy, because how many cores the cluster has could not be read. Each query adds its whole CPU seconds when it finishes: those under a second do not count, and a long one appears all at once at the end.
CPU time the queries spent, in CPU seconds: one second per second is one core busy. It is shown this way because, without the jmx catalog, how many cores the cluster has is unknown.
Tiempo de CPU que gastaron los trabajos: CPU time the jobs submitted in the last 5 minutes spent, summed across all threads, so it can exceed the 5 minutes.
Tiempo de CPU que usaron las consultas s: CPU time the queries on the regions used, as a share of the data nodes' cores (or the standalone server's): 100 % equals all busy with queries.
Tiempo de CPU que usaron las sentencias,: CPU time the statements used, as a share of all the server's cores: 100 % equals all busy with statements. High and sustained usually comes from queries without a suitable index or large sorts.
Tiempo de CPU que usaron las sesiones de: CPU time the database's sessions used, spread across the CPUs the instance can use (cpu_count or, if absent, the machine's). 100 % equals all those CPUs busy with this database; near that value, queries wait for CPU.
Tiempo de CPU que usaron las tareas de S: CPU time the SQL Server tasks used, spread across its visible schedulers (one per CPU it can use): 100 % equals all those CPUs busy with SQL Server. Unlike SQL Server CPU, it does not wait for the per-minute sample.
Tiempo de CPU que usaron los engines de: CPU time the ASE engines used, as a share of all of them (each engine uses one CPU at a time): 100 % equals all engines busy.
Tiempo de cómputo de las tareas de las c: Compute time of the tasks of the queries finished in the last 15 minutes, summed across all cores, so it can exceed the 15 minutes. It is the closest to the warehouse's consumption the API gives.
Tiempo de slot que consumieron los jobs: Slot time consumed by the jobs finished in the last 15 minutes, summed across all their slots. Divided by 900,000 ms it gives, approximately, the window's average slots (without the jobs still running).
Tiempo desde el último arranque de la ba: Time since the database last started.
Tiempo desde la última transacción que e: Time since the last transaction this replica applied, in seconds. If the primary does not write, it grows even though the replica is up to date.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el DataNode cuy: Time since the DataNode whose metrics endpoint is queried started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el JVM de este: Time since this server's JVM started. If it returns to zero, Solr restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el Master activ: Time since the active HBase Master started. If it returns to zero, it restarted or the Master changed.
Time since the coordinator started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el drillbit al: Time since the drillbit DBine connects to started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el entorno de M: Time since the Materialize environment started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el nodo más ant: Time since the oldest node in the cluster started. If it returns to zero, all of them restarted.
Time since the oldest node started.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el nodo que lle: Time since the node with the least uptime started. If it returns to zero, a node restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el primer dnode: Time since the first dnode taosKeeper returns started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el proceso del: Time since the process of the node this session is connected to started. If it returns to zero, the node restarted.
Time since the server process started. If it returns to zero, the server restarted.
Time since the server process started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el proceso etcd: Time since this member's etcd process started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el proceso infl: Time since the influxd process started. If it returns to zero, the server restarted.
Time since the influxdb3 process started. If it returns to zero, the server restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el servicio de: Time since the SQL Server service started.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el servidor Pos: Time since Babelfish's PostgreSQL server started.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el servidor de: Time since the database server started.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el servidor, se: Time since the server started, based on when tempdb was recreated.
Tiempo desde que arrancó el servidor. Si: Time since the server started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó este nodo de Co: Time since this CouchDB node started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó este nodo, segú: Time since this node started, based on its gossip generation. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó este nodo. Si v: Time since this node started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó la JVM de Neo4j: Time since the Neo4j JVM started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Tiempo desde que arrancó la instancia de: Time since the Neptune instance DBine connects to started. If it returns to zero, it restarted.
Time since the TiDB instance DBine is connected to started.
Tiempo desde que el motor abrió esta bas: Time since the engine opened this database, based on the oldest system connection. In Classic mode there are no system connections and it is not reported.
Tiempo desde que se activó la base, con: Time since the database was activated, by the first connection or with ACTIVATE DATABASE.
Tiempo en el que terminó el 99 % de los: Time within which 99 % of the HTTP requests of the last statistics window finished: it shows the slow requests the average hides.
Tiempo entre el último log que escribió: Time between the last log the primary wrote and the last one it sent to the secondary, on the most delayed service. If it grows, the secondary falls behind, and in a takeover those changes would be missing.
Tiempo medio de cada commit del backend: Average time of each backend (bbolt) commit to disk, averaged since the process started. It should be below 25 ms; more indicates a slow or heavily loaded disk.
Tiempo medio que CouchDB tardó en resolv: Average time CouchDB took to resolve HTTP requests in the last statistics window (10 s by default), not counting the network. If it rises, the node is loaded or there are slow views or queries.
Tiempo medio que tarda en llegar a disco: Average time each WAL write takes to reach disk, averaged since the process started, so it reacts slowly. It should be well below 10 ms; if it rises, the disk is slow for etcd and leader elections and slow requests appear.
Tiempo que el motor dedicó a ejecutar la: Time the engine spent running the queries finished in the last 15 minutes, summed, without the queue wait.
Tiempo que la JVM pasó recolectando basu: Time the JVM spent collecting garbage, summing all collectors. If it takes a large share of each second, the heap is too small or queries reserve a lot of memory.
Tiempo que las lecturas y escrituras de: Time file reads and writes waited for the disk, summed across all: with several at once it can exceed 1000 ms per second. If it rises without I/O rising, the disk is responding slower.
Tiempo que las transacciones pasaron esp: Time transactions spent waiting for locks in the last full minute, summed across all. The most contended rows are in the lock waits table.
Tiempo que lleva en marcha el nodo más a: How long the oldest node in the cluster has been running. If it drops suddenly, that node restarted.
Tiempo que pasó el JVM recolectando basu: Time the JVM spent collecting garbage, all collectors summed. If it grows fast, the heap is too small for the load and the pauses slow down searches.
Time the JVM spent collecting garbage, all collectors and nodes summed. If it grows fast, the heap is too small for the load and the pauses slow down searches.

Trabajos esperando un worker libre. Si n: Jobs waiting for a free worker. If it does not return to zero, searchd cannot keep up.

Cambiar el tablespace copia la base ente: Changing the tablespace copies the whole database to the new one: it takes as long as its size requires, needs nobody connected to it and locks it while it lasts.
Cambiar entre manual y autoescalado camb: Switching between manual and autoscale changes how you are billed: autoscale bills every hour for the highest RU/s it reached, at a higher per-RU/s rate than manual. The change can take a while to complete.
Cambiar la política de desalojo reinicia: Changing the eviction policy restarts the bucket: it stops serving for a moment and reloads the data from disk.
Cambiar la región principal mueve los le: Changing the primary region moves the leaseholders of the global and regional-by-default tables.
Cambiar la replicación mueve los datos e: Changing replication moves data in the background (tablets) and can take a while; when raising the factor, restart the applications so they see the new replicas.

Cambiar la supervivencia vuelve a ubicar: Changing survivability relocates the replicas of the whole database: with REGION, writes start waiting across regions.
Cambiar las réplicas crea o mueve vnodes: Changing the replicas creates or moves vnodes between dnodes: it copies the data of each vgroup and loads the cluster while it lasts.

Con DEFINER, el código nuevo corre con l: With DEFINER, the new code runs with its owner's permissions, even if the caller has fewer: it is a security risk.

Con facturación física se pagan también: With physical billing you also pay for the bytes kept by time travel (what was changed or deleted). If you don't need to go back more than 2 days, lowering the window to 48 hours reduces that cost.

Con flush activo, cualquiera con permiso: With flush enabled, anyone with permission can delete all documents at once.

Espacio que ocupan en disco los índices: Disk space taken by the indexes of this server's cores.
Espacio que ocupan en los nodos los shar: Space the index shards take on the nodes, primaries and replicas included.
Espacio que ocupan las columnas de todas: Space the columns of all tables take, system ones too, with their auxiliary structures: heaps, hashes, imprints and order indexes.

Espacio que ocupan los datos en los arch: Space the data in the attached databases' files takes: used blocks times their size, without free blocks or the WAL.
Espacio que ocupan los datos en los disc: Space the data takes on the backends' disks, replicas included; the maximum is the total capacity of those disks.
Espacio que ocupan los extents de datos: Space the data extents of all tables take.

La que usan las consultas que no empieza: The one used by queries that don't start with CYPHER 5 or CYPHER 25.

Las filas fuera del orden de la sort key: Rows out of sort key order force reading more blocks. VACUUM reorders them and reclaims the space of deleted ones.
Las operaciones mínimamente registradas: Minimally logged operations (SELECT INTO, fast bcp) break the log dump chain: after one, a DUMP DATABASE is needed before DUMP TRANSACTION can be done again.

Las partes separadas no se consultan per: Detached parts aren't queried but still take up disk space in detached/. Those the server set aside (broken, unexpected…) may be data missing from the table: review them before deleting. Those detached by hand are added back with ATTACH PART.
Las propiedades de la base (como replica: The database's properties (such as replication_allocation) are those of new tables; some, like binlog.enable, also affect existing ones.
Las que escriben a disco no van con un b: Those that write to disk don't go with an ephemeral bucket.
Las regiones actuales y una nueva al fin: The current regions and a new one at the end, comma-separated. One region is added at a time and they can't be removed.
Las réplicas de las tablas sin política: The replicas of tables without their own policy move to wherever the new one says: it can generate a lot of traffic between nodes.
Las réplicas nuevas (o las que se quitan: New replicas (or those being removed) aren't created until the cluster is rebalanced (Rebalance); meanwhile, the bucket keeps the previous number.
Las sesiones nuevas en la base empiezan: New sessions on the database start in read-only mode: they won't be able to write unless they change it in the session.
Las tablas borradas con DROP TABLE queda: Tables dropped with DROP TABLE stay in the recycle bin (BIN$…) and keep taking up space until Oracle needs it or they are purged. Purging is permanent: they can no longer be recovered with FLASHBACK TABLE … TO BEFORE DROP.
Las tablas columnares no necesitan estad: Columnar tables don't need statistics, but virtual ones (from a remote source) do: without them the optimizer doesn't know how many rows they bring and may choose wrong where to do the joins. Creating a HISTOGRAM one on the filter columns helps more.
Las tablas en CSV, JSON, Parquet u otros: Tables in CSV, JSON, Parquet or other formats have no transactions, time travel, OPTIMIZE or file skipping by statistics: every query reads everything. Parquet ones are converted to Delta in place with CONVERT TO DELTA; the others, with CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT.

Las tareas programadas no se registran d: Scheduled tasks aren't registered from a development build: use the installed app.

Lo que se escribe en una tabla columnar: What is written to a columnar table goes first to the delta store, which takes more memory and is slower to read than the main one. Automatic merge empties it; if it grew large, merge it by hand (it uses CPU and memory while it runs).

Memoria de la caché de nodos de B-tree d: Memory of the B-tree node cache of the database files, out of its maximum.
Memoria de las memtables: escrituras rec: Memtable memory: writes received that have not been flushed to SSTables on disk yet.
Memoria que usa DuckDB dentro de DBine,: Memory DuckDB uses inside DBine, summed across its components (database buffers, in-memory tables, indexes, running operations), out of its limit (memory_limit). Near the limit, queries spill data to disk or fail for lack of memory.
Memoria que usa DuckDB dentro del servid: Memory DuckDB uses inside the server, summed across its components (buffers, in-memory tables, indexes…), out of its limit (memory_limit). Near the limit, queries spill to disk or fail for lack of memory.
Memoria que usa SQLite en el proceso, su: Memory SQLite uses in the process, summing all SQLite databases open in DBine and not just this one, out of the peak it reached.
Memoria que usa el proceso de openGauss: Memory the openGauss process uses against max_process_memory. If it reaches the cap, new statements fail for lack of memory.
Memoria que usa la base como porcentaje: Memory the database uses as a percentage of its service tier limit, averaged over the last 15 s. It includes the data cache, so a high value is normal.
Memory the database uses as a percentage of the limit Fabric sets for it, averaged over the last 15 s. It includes the data cache, so a high value is normal.
Memoria que usa la instancia de TiDB a l: Memory the TiDB instance DBine is connected to uses. The maximum is tidb_server_memory_limit (or total memory, without a limit); near it, TiDB cancels the query using the most memory.
Memoria que usa la máquina virtual Erlan: Memory the Erlang virtual machine CouchDB runs on uses: processes, binaries, code, ETS tables, atoms and the rest. If it grows without stopping, look at which of those parts is growing.
Memoria que usan ahora las consultas en: Memory the running queries of the current database use now.
Memoria que usan ahora las sesiones del: Memory the sessions of the query node DBine is connected to use now, summed; does not include the caches or the rest of the process.
Memoria que usan los nodos de GreptimeDB: Memory the GreptimeDB nodes use, summed; the maximum is the total memory they have.
Memoria que usan los nodos del cluster,: Memory the cluster's nodes use, summed; the maximum is the sum of their maximum_memory. Near the maximum, queries asking for more memory fail.
Memoria que usan los pools de memoria de: Memory Db2's memory pools use (buffer pools, sort heap, package cache…) on all members; the maximum is the host's memory.
Memoria que usan los procesos de la inst: Memory the instance's processes use, summed; does not include the shared globals buffers.

Memory the instance's processes use: in-memory tables, query computations, code and shared memory. The maximum is the allocation limit (global_allocation_limit); near it, HANA unloads tables from memory and statements may fail for lack of memory.
Memoria que usan los procesos de los bac: Memory the backends' processes use, summed; the maximum is the sum of their memory limits (mem_limit). Near the limit, queries asking for more memory fail.
Memoria que usan los procesos yb-tserver: Memory the yb-tserver processes use, summed across nodes, against their limit. Near the limit, the tservers start throttling and rejecting writes.
Memoria que usan todas las réplicas de c: Memory all cluster replicas use, summed, against what their sizes allocate.
Mientras siga abierta, las versiones vie: While it stays open, old record versions can't be cleaned up and the database grows and gets slower. Find the connection in MON$TRANSACTIONS (the one with MON$TRANSACTION_ID = {0}) and close it or end its transaction. {1}

Muchos VLF hacen lentos el arranque, la: Many VLFs make startup, restore and log backups slow. They are reduced by shrinking the log and growing it in large steps.

MyISAM no tiene transacciones ni recuper: MyISAM has no transactions or crash recovery, locks the whole table on every write and ignores foreign keys. Converting it to InnoDB rewrites the table: on large tables, do it outside business hours.
Más de un 20 % de filas muertas: la tabl: More than 20 % dead rows: the table takes up more than it needs and reads walk through rows that no longer exist. If it recurs, autovacuum isn't enough: check for long transactions or lower autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor on those tables.
Más retención ocupa más almacenamiento;: More retention takes more storage; with less, data can no longer be read or restored further back than the new period.
Mínimo 1h. Vale para los grupos de shard: Minimum 1h. Applies to new shard groups.

Porcentaje de accesos a bloques que se r: Percentage of block accesses resolved in the buffer pool without reading the disk, accumulated since startup. If it drops, a larger buffer pool (-B) is advisable.
Porcentaje de accesos a páginas de índic: Percentage of index page accesses that did not have to read the disk, accumulated since startup.
Porcentaje de aciertos de la caché de da: Data cache hit rate, accumulated since startup.
Porcentaje de aciertos de los buffer poo: Buffer pool hit rate, averaged across them and accumulated since startup.
Porcentaje de autenticaciones resueltas: Percentage of authentications resolved with the user cache, accumulated since startup. Low indicates many requests have to look up the user in _users, which adds latency.
Porcentaje de bloques encontrados en sha: Percentage of blocks found in shared_buffers without asking the operating system, accumulated since the last statistics reset, so it changes slowly. What is not found may still come from the operating system cache.
Porcentaje de bloques leídos que ya esta: Percentage of blocks read that were already in shared_buffers, accumulated since the last statistics reset, so it changes slowly. In a transactional load, below ~99 % usually means memory is lacking or there are scans of large tables.
Porcentaje de búsquedas en documentCache: Percentage of documentCache lookups (the stored fields of documents already read) that found the document, accumulated since the cores were loaded. If low, every response re-reads the documents from the index.
Porcentaje de búsquedas en filterCache (: Percentage of filterCache lookups (the documents that meet each fq filter) that found the result, accumulated since the cores were loaded. If low with filters that repeat, the cache is too small.
Porcentaje de búsquedas en la caché de c: Percentage of lookups in the query cache (filters) that found the result, accumulated since the nodes started, so it changes slowly. It is common for it to be low: only filters that repeat, on large segments, are stored.
Porcentaje de búsquedas en la caché de m: Percentage of lookups in the marks cache (each MergeTree part's index) that found what they sought, accumulated since startup, hence it changes slowly. If it drops, mark_cache_size is too small for the tables being queried.
Porcentaje de búsquedas en queryResultCa: Percentage of queryResultCache lookups (the sorted results of repeated queries) that found the result, accumulated since the cores were loaded. It is normal for it to be low if queries almost never repeat.
Porcentaje de las búsquedas en la caché: Percentage of key cache lookups that found where the partition is without reading the index from disk, accumulated since startup. Low with many reads suggests raising key_cache_size.
Porcentaje de las lecturas de documentos: Percentage of document reads (gets) resolved in memory, without going to disk, in the data service's latest sample. Low indicates the documents being read do not fit in the buckets' RAM quota.
Porcentaje de las lecturas de nodos de B: Percentage of B-tree node reads resolved with the cache, accumulated since startup. Low indicates more pages are read from disk than necessary.
Porcentaje de las lecturas resueltas con: Percentage of reads resolved with the row cache, accumulated since startup. Low indicates the data being read does not fit in memory and is fetched from the SSTables.
Percentage of reads resolved with the row cache, accumulated since startup. Only appears if the row cache is enabled.
Porcentaje de las páginas pedidas a la c: Percentage of pages requested from the WiredTiger cache that were already in memory, accumulated since startup. Low or falling indicates the data being queried does not fit in the cache and is read from disk.
Porcentaje de lecturas de bloques que en: Percentage of block reads that found the block in the storage cache (Pebble) of this session's node, accumulated since it started, so it changes slowly. If it drops, the data read often does not fit in the cache.
Porcentaje de lecturas de bloques resuel: Percentage of block reads resolved in the buffer cache without going to disk, in the last minute (in a PDB, since startup). A sustained drop indicates a cache too small for the load or queries scanning huge tables.
Porcentaje de lecturas de la caché que e: Percentage of cache reads that found the page without going to disk, in the current database and accumulated since it was opened.
Porcentaje de lecturas de páginas de Inn: Percentage of InnoDB page reads resolved in the buffer pool without going to disk, accumulated since startup, hence it changes slowly. If it drops, the buffer pool is too small for the data being queried.
Porcentaje de lecturas de páginas de dat: Percentage of data and index page reads resolved in the buffer pools, accumulated since the database was activated. If it drops, the buffer pools are too small.
Porcentaje de lecturas de páginas que se: Percentage of page reads resolved in the buffers without going to disk, accumulated since startup or since the last onstat -z. If it drops, buffers are lacking.
Porcentaje de lecturas lógicas que encon: Percentage of logical reads that found the page in the data caches, accumulated since startup. If it drops, the caches are too small.
Porcentaje de los shards del cluster que: Percentage of the cluster's shards that are active. Below 100 %, there are shards unassigned or recovering.
Porcentaje de pedidos de SQL y PL/SQL qu: Percentage of SQL and PL/SQL requests that found their already-parsed version in the library cache, in the last minute. If it drops, it is usually due to many hard parses or a small shared pool. In a PDB it is empty: Oracle does not report V$SYSMETRIC there.
Porcentaje de pedidos de páginas que se: Percentage of page requests resolved in the buffer without reading the disk, accumulated since startup.
Porcentaje de pedidos que encontraron su: Percentage of requests that found their result in each shard's request cache (searches with size=0, such as aggregations), accumulated since the nodes started. It drops if indexes change often, because each refresh invalidates it.
Porcentaje de páginas encontradas en el: Percentage of pages found in the buffer pool without reading from disk, over the last thousands of accesses. It is usually near 100 %; to see memory pressure, page life expectancy is more useful.
Porcentaje de páginas pedidas que ya est: Percentage of requested pages that were already in the cache, accumulated since the database was opened, hence it changes slowly. If it drops steadily, the page cache is too small for what is queried.
Porcentaje de páginas que se encontraron: Percentage of pages found in the buffer pool without reading the disk, according to SQL Server's counter. If it drops steadily, memory is lacking for the data being queried.
Posición actual del WAL, en bytes: su av: Current WAL position, in bytes: its advance is the volume of changes the server generates, what the replicas receive and what is archived.
Promover automáticamente archivos y carp: Automatically promote files and folders to datasets
Páginas en uso de la base; el máximo es: Pages in use in the database; the maximum is the total number of pages in its files.
Páginas que pidieron las sentencias, est: Pages the statements requested, whether or not in the cache: measures how much read work the database does.
Páginas, modificadas o no, que WiredTige: Pages, modified or not, that WiredTiger removes from the cache to make room. A high, sustained rate indicates pressure on the cache.
Quitar los datasets que ya no existen en: Remove datasets that no longer exist in the source
Quitar una región mueve sus réplicas y s: Removing a region moves its replicas and data to the database's other regions.
Qué hace el servidor cuando dos escritur: What the server does when two writes change the same record at once.
RESTRICTED deja las réplicas de las tabl: RESTRICTED keeps the replicas of regional tables only in their region.
RESTRICTED quita las réplicas no votante: RESTRICTED removes non-voting replicas from other regions: reads from them stop being local.
RU/s máximas: «{0}» no es un valor válid: Maximum RU/s: “{0}” is not a valid value (from 1000, in steps of 1000)
RU/s: «{0}» no es un valor válido (desde: RU/s: “{0}” is not a valid value (from 400, in steps of 100)
Rechaza UPDATE y DELETE sin WHERE. Vacío: Rejects UPDATE and DELETE without WHERE. Empty: RESET.
Replaces the whole security object. If members ends up with no names or roles, the database is public: anyone can read and write documents. Removing names or roles leaves those who used them without access.
Registra la versión de intercalación del: Records the operating system's or ICU's collation version as the database's. Applied once; it isn't left marked.
Registrar sentencias que tarden más de (: Log statements that take longer than (log_min_duration_statement)
Retención extra del WAL para suscripcion: Extra WAL retention for subscriptions (WAL_RETENTION_PERIOD, s)
RisingWave 2.5 o posterior, con licencia: RisingWave 2.5 or later, licensed. Empty: the system's (DEFAULT).
Réplicas de shards que todavía no están: Shard replicas not yet assigned or synchronized. The data stays available, but with fewer copies than configured.
Réplicas en un estado distinto de active: Replicas in a state other than active, such as down, recovering or recovery_failed. While recovering it is normal; if they stay that way, that part of the index has fewer copies or does not respond.
SINGLE_USER o RESTRICTED_USER cierran la: SINGLE_USER or RESTRICTED_USER close the other sessions; with SINGLE_USER, the next session to connect can take the database over.
SKIP solo cambia un paso que todavía no: SKIP only changes a step that has not started yet, and {0} is in {1}.
SQL SECURITY: «{0}» no es DEFINER ni INV: SQL SECURITY: “{0}” is neither DEFINER nor INVOKER
SQLite aceptó los cambios pero no aplicó: SQLite accepted the changes but didn't apply all of them: {0}
Sale de la cuota libre del cluster. Míni: Comes out of the cluster's free quota. Minimum 100 MB (Magma: 1024 MB before 7.6).
Se aplica con VACUUM, que reescribe la b: Applied with VACUUM, which rewrites the whole database: it locks it while it runs and needs free disk space the size of the database.
Se aplica con VACUUM. En modo WAL no cam: Applied with VACUUM. In WAL mode it doesn't change: switch the journal to DELETE first (can be done in the same change).
Se transfiere con GRANT OWNERSHIP … COPY: Transferred with GRANT OWNERSHIP … COPY CURRENT GRANTS.
Based on the history the engine keeps. Backups made with other tools outside the server don't appear.
Separadas por comas. La principal solo s: Comma-separated. The primary one can only be removed when it is the last; then the database stops being multi-region.
Si la base ya supera la nueva cuota, se: If the database already exceeds the new quota, new loads and inserts are rejected until space is freed.
Si la retención nueva es más corta, se b: If the new retention is shorter, data older than it is deleted in the next retention pass.
If the new retention is shorter, data older than it is deleted.
Si la vida nueva es más corta, los datos: If the new lifetime is shorter, data older than it stops being visible and is deleted in the next compaction.
Si los datos viejos dejan de servir pasa: If old data stops being useful after a while, a TTL deletes it (or moves it to a cheaper disk) on its own, instead of growing without limit. Ignore it if the table has to keep the whole history.
Si los datos viejos dejan de servir, un: If old data stops being useful, partition expiry deletes it on its own instead of paying for its storage forever. Ignore it if the table has to keep the whole history; the days are your decision.
Si se achica, los consumidores de suscri: If it is reduced, lagging subscription consumers may lose data.
Si se acorta, los consumidores de suscri: If it is shortened, lagging subscription consumers may lose data.
Si se desactiva, nadie podrá conectarse: If turned off, nobody will be able to connect to the database (not even DBine to explore it) until it is turned back on.
SimpleStrategy ignora los datacenters: s: SimpleStrategy ignores datacenters: only for a single-datacenter cluster.
Sin autovacuum las filas muertas no se l: Without autovacuum, dead rows aren't cleaned, statistics go stale and the database approaches the transaction limit (wraparound). It also needs track_counts. On a managed service it's changed in the instance parameters.
Sin checkpoint al recuperar (no chkpt on: No checkpoint on recovery (no chkpt on recovery)
Sin clave primaria el motor usa una clav: Without a primary key the engine uses a hidden internal key, nothing prevents duplicate rows and, with row-based replication, every UPDATE or DELETE scans the whole table on the replicas. Group Replication and sql_require_primary_key require one.
Sin clave primaria nada impide filas dup: Without a primary key nothing prevents duplicate rows, logical replication can't publish its UPDATEs and DELETEs, and tools (including DBine's data editing) can't identify a row.
Sin clave primaria no hay forma segura d: Without a primary key there is no safe way to identify a row: data editing, replication (Enterprise Replication requires it) and comparisons get complicated.
Without a primary key there is no safe way to identify a row: data editing, replication (GoldenGate, logical Data Guard) and comparisons get complicated.

Sin contabilidad de espacio libre (no fr: No free space accounting (no free space acctg)
Sin contabilidad de espacio libre no se: Without free space accounting, the thresholds of data segments don't fire.
Sin escrituras durables (durable_writes: Without durable writes (durable_writes = false) writes don't go through the commit log: if a node goes down, whatever wasn't on disk yet is lost.
Sin escrituras forzadas el sistema opera: Without forced writes the operating system delays writes: a power cut or system crash can corrupt the database. Turn them on from the server with gfix -write sync <database>.
Sin estadísticas al día el optimizador e: Without up-to-date statistics the optimizer misestimates rows and picks slow plans.
Sin estadísticas el optimizador no sabe: Without statistics the optimizer doesn't know how many rows the table has and can pick bad plans. Run UPDATE STATISTICS (LOW for all; MEDIUM or HIGH on filter columns) or schedule it with the automatic task.
Sin estadísticas el optimizador supone c: Without statistics the optimizer assumes row counts and can pick slow plans.
Sin estadísticas el optimizador supone t: Without statistics the optimizer assumes default sizes and can pick very bad plans. Automatic collection gathers them over time; if it's off, run RUNSTATS.
Sin estadísticas, o con más de 10 % de f: Without statistics, or with more than 10 % of rows changed since the last ones, the optimizer misestimates and picks slow plans. The automatic maintenance task gathers them overnight; if it's off or the table changes a lot during the day, gather them by hand.
Sin fusión automática el delta store sol: Without automatic merge, the delta store is only emptied with MERGE DELTA. Fine if a load does it by hand when done; otherwise it grows without limit.
Sin la cantidad de CPU del host (ENV_GET: Without the host's CPU count (ENV_GET_SYSTEM_RESOURCES) the database's CPU time is not shown.
Sin la cantidad de engines (master..syse: Without the number of engines (master..sysengines) the CPU time is not shown.
Sin la cantidad de procesadores del equi: Without the machine's processor count (sysmaster:sysmachineinfo) the CPU time is not shown.
Sin log no hay ROLLBACK ni recuperación: Without a log there is no ROLLBACK or recovery of what was committed after the last backup. With buffering, a crash can lose the latest committed transactions. The mode is changed with ondblog or ontape and a level 0 backup, not with SQL.
Sin sysadmin ni monadmin, solo incluye t: Without sysadmin or monadmin, it only includes your sessions.
Sin tabla de destino, la consulta es DDL: With no destination table, the query is DDL, DML or a script: each run makes its changes again.
Sin tablas con muchas filas desordenadas: No tables with many unsorted rows
Sin tablas con muchas filas muertas: No tables with many dead rows
Sin tablas con mucho espacio libre sin u: No tables with a lot of unused free space
Sin validación, se guardan registros que: Without validation, records that don't meet the schema's constraints (required, not null, minimum, maximum…) are saved.
